title: Move a project through a portfolio
description: Make a bespoke lifecycle visible, with permitted moves and probabilistic runs.
try_this: Add a project, inspect its permitted next states, then compare one journey with the batch summary.
limitation: An invented transition model; frequencies illustrate supplied probabilities rather than predict a real portfolio.
image_alt: View of the move a project through a portfolio example

title: See a project from different seats
description: Compare stakeholder priorities, influence and sentiment through role-specific views.
try_this: Switch your role, inspect the stakeholder measures, and compare the charts with the source table.
limitation: Illustrative assessments and relationships, not surveyed evidence or a computed stakeholder strategy.
image_alt: View of the see a project from different seats example

title: Read a stakeholder concept schema
description: Explore the concepts and partial relationships in a draft stakeholder model.
try_this: Select a concept, read its incoming and outgoing relationships, then inspect concepts with no links yet.
limitation: A partial concept schema, not a measured social network. Unconnected concepts are visible gaps; positions and colours do not measure influence.
image_alt: View of the explore stakeholder relationships example

title: Trace outputs towards benefits
description: Explore an illustrative East West Rail scope-to-benefit tree.
try_this: Select nodes and follow the links from outputs through outcomes to benefits. Move nodes to make a relationship easier to read.
limitation: A teaching example inspired by the railway, not an approved scope or evidence that benefits will occur.
image_alt: View of the trace outputs towards benefits example

title: Olaf’s afternoon deliveries
description: Turn a small request into visible counts and individual confirmations.
try_this: Count the deliveries, correct a count, and check each person out to complete the fictional checklist.
limitation: Page-local state only. Completing a checklist cannot establish that a real site is safe to close.
image_alt: View of the olaf’s afternoon deliveries example

title: Find the kind of decision you are making
description: Use an ontology-inspired questionnaire to distinguish decision objects, statements and processes.
try_this: Try the same situation as a decision to be made and as an existing decision statement; compare the resulting paths.
limitation: A guide to useful distinctions, not an automatic decision maker or a complete ontology reasoner.
image_alt: View of the find the kind of decision you are making example

title: Find a better trade-off together
description: Compare allocation along a frontier with an illustrative outward change in what is possible.
try_this: Explore the points and the two objectives. Distinguish a better position on a frontier from improving the feasible options.
limitation: A drawn, illustrative frontier. The app does not derive an optimum, establish orthogonality or prove a win-win is feasible.
image_alt: View of the find a better trade-off together example

title: When do task delays happen together?
description: Separate each task’s delay distribution from their joint dependence.
try_this: Inspect the fixed marginal distributions, change the Gaussian dependence parameter and sample size, then compare the scatter and tail summaries.
limitation: Synthetic draws and a Gaussian copula. Its parameter is not generally the Pearson correlation of the displayed delays; extreme-tail dependence is not represented.
image_alt: View of the when do task delays happen together? example

title: A project review changes the next move
description: Walk through a scripted project narrative using prediction error and active-inference language as an analogy.
try_this: Advance through the reviews and compare the beliefs, progress, recorded decisions and later outcomes.
limitation: Scripted teaching values, not variational or expected free-energy calculations, inferred policies or a validated Active Inference model.
image_alt: View of the a project review changes the next move example

title: A software team learns and reworks
description: Explore assumed feedback between delivery, learning, debt, reviews, scope and morale.
try_this: Advance a week, switch effects off and on, then run and reset. Read the event log alongside the trajectory.
limitation: Invented stochastic rules and coefficients, not calibrated project forecasts. Reset keeps your effect choices.
image_alt: View of the a software team learns and reworks example
original_notes: Real projects are not just made up of task nodes connected by dependency edges. There are regular circles of daily activities, monthly progress review actions, etc. There is negative feedback pushing back on attempted initiatives, and positive reinforcing loops sometimes triggered after the first or second task is done.

title: A day on the pool-and-gym site
description: Read and run a downloadable NetLogo model of workers and deliveries over one day.
try_this: Download the model, load it into NetLogo Web, set worker count, then run setup and go.
limitation: A small occupancy illustration with fixed schedules. It cannot establish safe staffing, site capacity or construction logistics.
image_alt: View of the a day on the pool-and-gym site example

title: Discuss data maturity in context
description: Inspect maturity stages, dimensions and their connections to organisational capabilities.
try_this: Compare the question bank in graph and table views. Filter by capability or level and open the detailed questions to discuss what evidence an answer would need.
limitation: A supplied discussion framework, not a validated assessment instrument or an evidence-based score for your organisation.
image_alt: View of the discuss data maturity in context example

title: Find your way into project controls
description: Explore the discipline’s relationships and a separate eight-step learning route for a project manager.
try_this: Search or filter, inspect a concept and its real links, then follow the learning route.
limitation: Curated concepts and predicates. Teaching order is a suggested reading path, not an additional set of graph relationships.
image_alt: View of the find your way into project controls example

title: Match a task to a capability
description: Explore an earlier proposal for connecting task needs with AI capabilities and model choices.
try_this: Focus or select a capability, read its description, and follow its connections.
limitation: A historical conceptual map, not a current model ranking, benchmark or proof that the suggested combination works.
image_alt: View of the match a task to a capability example

title: Follow the changing project-tool landscape
description: Read a sourced timeline alongside an interpretation of software branches and convergences.
try_this: Explore a branch or milestone, compare its description, and distinguish dated product events from broader trends.
limitation: Selected events and an interpretive arrangement; connections are not evidence of product inheritance or a forecast.
image_alt: View of the follow the changing project-tool landscape example

title: Imagine different project-services markets
description: Explore a speculative scenario for how capabilities and business models could change.
try_this: Move along the timeline and compare the market, services and implications at each imagined stage.
limitation: Hypothetical future milestones and dates, not forecasts of AGI, ASI or market demand.
image_alt: View of the imagine different project-services markets example

title: Build and interpret a risk matrix
description: Place several risks on a likelihood–impact grid and inspect the rule behind its bands.
try_this: Add delayed materials at likelihood 3 and impact 5, then edit likelihood to 4. Add another risk in the same square.
limitation: Ordinal scores and colour bands are conventions, not probabilities, expected losses or proof that a risk is acceptable.
image_alt: View of the build and interpret a risk matrix example

title: Compare options with weighted criteria
description: Make criteria, weights and scores explicit, then inspect how the ranking changes.
try_this: Raise the affordability weight to 0.7 and inspect the three-way tie. Change it again to reverse the ranking.
limitation: A compensatory weighted sum of supplied judgements; it does not discover evidence, enforce mandatory constraints or select the right option for you.
image_alt: View of the compare options with weighted criteria example

title: Sort tasks by urgency and importance
description: Place tasks on two distinct axes and reconsider their suggested next actions.
try_this: Add the examples and move Plan recovery drills from urgency 2 to 3 without changing its importance.
limitation: The midpoint is a chosen convention; suggested actions do not establish capacity, delegability or what a person ought to value.
image_alt: View of the sort tasks by urgency and importance example

title: Trace decisions beside overlapping work
description: Compare task dates and decision response times in an illustrative knowledge-graph project.
try_this: Select Security review, then select a task bar. Trace the associations across both charts; clear the selection to restore the whole picture.
limitation: Illustrative dates and elapsed decision times. No dated decisions, causal gating rules or dependency network are supplied, so the chart cannot attribute schedule delay or calculate a critical path.
image_alt: View of the trace decisions beside overlapping work example

title: Find the delay that moves the finish
description: Change durations and watch total float, critical routes and project completion respond.
try_this: Add one unit to A, reset, then add one to B. One uses float; the other moves completion.
limitation: A deterministic finish-to-start network, without calendars, resources, lags, uncertainty or costs.
image_alt: View of the find the delay that moves the finish example

title: Follow work into products
description: Explore the same illustrative railway through its process and deliverable hierarchies and their mappings.
try_this: Expand the trees and select Old Oak Common foundations on the work side. Follow its distinct product, then change phase to compare the supplied metrics.
limitation: Unverified legacy HS2 teaching inputs with no reliable reporting date. The left tree is a process hierarchy, not a standards-conformant WBS; metrics are supplied separately, not calculated roll-ups.
image_alt: View of the follow work into products example
tags: WBS, PBS, moving_between_perspectives, output, scope, hs2

title: Check the shape and meaning of project data
description: Edit a fictional project record and inspect checks on dates, costs, funding and provenance.
try_this: Complete a milestone early, then change a CAPEX funding currency and set tolerance to zero. Revalidate and compare the findings.
limitation: Illustrative checks, not official PDS validation or certification. Funding assumes whole-baseline coverage; provenance is declared, not independently verified.
image_alt: View of the check the shape and meaning of project data example

title: Explore gaps in a capability map
description: Edit six capability scores for five fictional firms, compare six pairwise plots and position an entrant in the empty regions.
try_this: Raise two scores for one firm to 10, then lower one. Watch the empty upper-right region close and reopen before moving the entrant sliders.
limitation: Invented scores and a 0.1-grid geometric search. Empty areas do not establish demand, feasibility, competitor capability or a commercial opportunity.
image_alt: View of the explore gaps in a capability map example

title: Separate capability, maturity and performance
description: Use a perceived need to suggest one lead service, then choose the portfolio, programme or project levels to address.
try_this: Choose Performance and apply its levels, then switch to Capability. Compare keeping those levels with applying the new suggestion.
limitation: A fixed conversation heuristic; it does not diagnose a project, perform a P3M3 assessment or validate a service’s suitability.
image_alt: View of the separate capability, maturity and performance example

title: Who needs a different conversation?
description: Map stakeholder influence and interest, revise your judgements, and inspect the suggested contact approach.
try_this: Raise Residents’ power from 30 to 70. Add a second stakeholder at the same position and inspect both.
limitation: Supplied judgements with a conventional split at 50. Scores do not measure support, rights or relationships, and low power does not justify exclusion.
image_alt: View of the who needs a different conversation? example
